newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia must limit credit to state firms - cenbank.
newsitem.headline: Croatia must limit credit to state firms - cenbank.

text.p: Croatia will have to tighten credit given by banks to some state firms in order to secure continued support from the International Monetary Fund (IMF), the National Bank of Croatia said on Monday.
An IMF mission has just completed its first visit here to review progress under a new $486 million aid programme approved in March.
The loan, the Extended Fund Facility (EFF), is designed to help Croatia overcome balance of payments difficulties and structural problems.

While overall economic performance remained within targets set under a government programme that runs to 1999, the IMF demanded further restrictions in the financing of 31 companies the government controls, the central bank said in a news release.
Restructuring and privatisation of the state-owned firms was outlined as another area where more speed was needed.
The bank said some firms still took advantage of their monopolistic position in the market to increase already high debts, while putting off steps to improve their own efficiency.

Therefore Croatia will have to draft and send to the IMF a new letter of intent featuring stricter measures to improve financial discipline before it can draw on the second tranche of the three-year loan, the bank said.

The fund's executive board is expected to discuss approval of the second tranche, totalling 28.8 million special drawing rights (SDRs) or around $40 million, in July. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
